NASA Black Marble 2016 — ending Earth night lights

Source: https://science.nasa.gov/earth/earth-observatory/earth-at-night/maps/
NASA Earth Observatory / Suomi NPP VIIRS; data processing by Miguel Roman, NASA GSFC.
Downloaded 2026-10-16. Original grayscale JPEGs retained unchanged:
- BlackMarble_2016_3km_gray.jpg: 13500 x 6750 global composite.
- BlackMarble_2016_B1_gray.jpg: 21600 x 21600, west 90..0, north 90..0 degrees.
- BlackMarble_2016_C1_gray.jpg: 21600 x 21600, east 0..90, north 90..0 degrees.

Download directory:
https://assets.science.nasa.gov/content/dam/science/esd/eo/images/imagerecords/144000/144897/

T_NASA_NightGlobal.png is an 8192 x 4096 resample of the global raster.
T_NASA_NightEurope.png is an 8192 x 8192 resample of the contiguous
-22.5..67.5 longitude / 90..0 latitude region from B1 and C1.
Reproduce via Scripts/prepare_ending_night_earth.py (Pillow).
No invented cities or roads have been painted into the data. Gold lighting,
contrast, clouds and blue atmospheric shading are artistic material treatments.

NASA Earth Science imagery is available for reuse, including commercial reuse,
except where a third-party copyright is identified; these NASA data maps do not
identify a third-party copyright. No NASA logos or endorsement are used.
https://science.nasa.gov/earth/faq/
https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/
Credit in project: NASA Earth Observatory / Suomi NPP VIIRS Black Marble 2016.
